from.place: Proof, final paragraph: an additive functor preserving kernels and cokernels preserves finite limits and finite colimits.

title: Kernel and cokernel criteria for finite exactness
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] and let $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive functor [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. If $H$ carries every kernel cone to a kernel cone, then $H$ preserves finite limits. If $H$ carries every cokernel cocone to a cokernel cocone, then $H$ preserves finite colimits. Preservation means carrying limiting cones, respectively colimiting cocones, to such cones and cocones [def-galois-exact-functor]. Here, for a morphism $f:X\to Y$, a kernel cone is a map $k:K\to X$ with $fk=0$ such that every map $a:P\to X$ with $fa=0$ has a unique factorization $a=ku$; a cokernel cocone is a map $q:Y\to Q$ with $qf=0$ such that every map $b:Y\to P$ with $bf=0$ has a unique factorization $b=vq$. Composition is written $ba=b\circ a$.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, proof of (2), paragraph beginning Conversely: finite products and equalizers as kernels of differences.
